entities.summary: Manuel Polo y Peyrolón (1846–1918) was a Spanish writer, theorist, academic, and politician. He is best known as the author of five novels falling in between romanticism and realism; classified as part of costumbrismo, they are currently considered second-rate literature. As a philosopher he stuck to neo-Thomism and focused mostly on confronting Krausism. In education he represented Catholic regenerationism, fiercely pitted against the Liberal current. In politics he was active within Carlism; his career reached its peak during his 1896–1898 term in the Congress of Deputies and his 1907-1915 terms in the Senate.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent figure in Spanish politics and education, Manuel Polo y Peyrolón's advocacy for Catholic regenerationism influenced the country's educational policies during his tenure in the Senate. His work also contributed to the development of costumbrismo, a literary movement that shaped Spanish literature between romanticism and realism.
